attribution.note: Zitron's own words, block-quoted from his July 28, 2026 newsletter and re-endorsed in this post.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the chain: purchases raise memory prices, which raise server costs, and weak AI revenue forces more debt. Calling it causal is correct.

contract.note: Reading hyperscalers as the four named firms and using Q2 2026 is ordinary and fair. Requiring evidence of a financing necessity, not just simultaneous trends, matches the word 'forced'.

evidence.note: TrendForce, Q2 2026: AI server demand drove HBM and RDIMM shipments, and DRAM contract prices rose. This backs one link. It says nothing about the four firms' AI finances or their borrowing.
TrendForce, Sept 29: HBM supply is tight and system costs are rising quickly. This backs the server-cost link but not the financing link.
Microsoft's own disclosure: cloud revenue up 27%. Cloud revenue includes non-AI services and covers only one of the four firms, so it cannot test the premise about incremental AI revenue.

reviews.rationale: The evidence backs the links from AI demand to memory prices and system costs. Nothing in the packet measures AI-attributable revenue or cash flow for the four firms, or shows that borrowing was forced rather than chosen. The Microsoft cloud figure does not isolate AI. The full causal chain cannot be decided.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: Unhedged present-tense language about eventual outcomes, framed in context as what will happen ('one day... runs out of money and dies'). 'For the most part' is preserved. A forecast with no deadline.

contract.note: Reading 'for the most part' as a majority by count of major AI startups other than OpenAI and Anthropic is an ordinary reading. The early-resolution rule appropriately requires terminal outcomes.

evidence.note: Cognition's own disclosure of a $48B funding round on Sept 8, 2026. A valuation reference only; it shows no terminal outcome.

reviews.rationale: This forecast has no deadline. The packet holds no terminal outcomes for any defined population of AI startups, so no conclusive event has settled a majority either way. A new funding round neither confirms nor refutes an indefinite forecast.

attribution.note: Zitron's own estimate in his newsletter.

semantics.note: 'I think it's fair to say' asserts an estimate with a firm 'at least 50%' threshold. It is not one of the listed probability hedges. The proposition keeps his framing.

contract.note: Using fiscal Q1 2027 (Oracle's latest quarter before the post) and recognized revenue attributable to OpenAI is a fair plain reading. The contract also notes, fairly, that CPU revenue is not automatically AI revenue.

evidence.note: Oracle's Q1 FY27 release: total revenue and cloud infrastructure revenue. It gives no AI-only total and no revenue figure for OpenAI.

reviews.rationale: The packet gives neither Oracle's AI-only revenue for the quarter nor the share coming from OpenAI. Total and cloud revenue cannot settle whether OpenAI accounts for at least 50% of AI revenue.

attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his newsletter.

semantics.note: The proposition keeps the claim that delays (power or construction) are causing pressure on 'effectively any' data-center debt. 'Effectively any' is kept as a scope term.

contract.note: Reading 'not getting built' as widespread delivery delays, not a literal absence of construction, is ordinary and generous. Reading 'effectively any' as nearly market-wide follows his wording. The two-month window comes from his own example.

evidence.note: A secondary summary of a Sept 25 BofA report: investors want wider premiums on AI project loans because of delays and power bottlenecks. It backs the narrow link only. CMBS spreads were flat that week, so market-wide pressure is not shown.
CBRE, H1 2026: record supply and record construction. Earlier period, and not limited to AI facilities. It argues against a literal reading but does not decide the window.

reviews.rationale: One secondary summary links delays to wider premiums on AI project loans. There is no representative evidence of widespread delivery failure, and no evidence of pressure across nearly all data-center debt; one week of flat CMBS spreads neither proves nor refutes that. The breadth the claim asserts is not settled.
